newsitem.title: USA: Fire sweeps through San Francisco apartments.
newsitem.headline: Fire sweeps through San Francisco apartments.

text.p: A fierce fire swept through an apartment complex on Wednesday, damaging scores of apartments, injuring five people and making hundreds homeless, fire officials said.
The fire broke out in one apartment and quickly spread to neighboring units of the two-story Country Club apartment complex in Fremont, 40 miles (70 kms) southeast of San Francisco.

About 90 firefighters from Fremont and several nearby cities helped put out the fire, Fremont Fire Department spokesman Dennis Satariano said. Eight residents had to be rescued from second-story balconies, he said.
Three apartment residents were treated at a local hospital -- a 91-year-old woman and a 41-year-old man suffering chest pains and a 40-year-old man who had a seizure, Satariano said.
Two firefighters were also taken to the hospital, one with eye injuries and another with smoke inhalation, he said.
Satariano said 68 apartments sustained varying degrees of fire, smoke or water damage and all were uninhabitable. At least two apartments were completely destroyed, he said.
Another 30 apartments in a separate wing of the complex suffered light smoke damage and may be uninhabitable, he said.
Satariano estimated that between 200 and 300 people had been made temporarily homeless by the blaze.
"The American Red Cross is opening an evacuation center and attempting to house the people," he added.
The cause of the fire was under investigation, he said. No monetary estimate of damage was immediately available, he said.
